title: Social Influence: Obedience & Milgram
welcome_lead: Pull the levers in Milgram's lab and learn why ordinary people obey.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology obedience: Milgram 1963 baseline 65%, agentic state, legitimacy of authority.
final_note: Obedience is built less from cruelty than from situation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Milgram (1963) told 40 male volunteers they were testing learning. The 'teacher' shocked a 'learner' up to 450 volts. 65% went to the maximum; 100% reached 300V. Despite obvious distress, the experimenter's prods kept most participants going.

Milgram explained results through the agentic state: participants shifted responsibility to the experimenter. This requires legitimacy of authority — Yale's status helped. When relocated to a run-down Bridgeport office, obedience fell to 47.5%.

Adorno et al. (1950) measured the authoritarian personality with the F-scale. High scorers were rigid, deferential to authority and hostile to out-groups — a dispositional explanation that contrasts with Milgram's situational one.
